summary: This clipped Wikipedia-style note is a collection of excerpts about Kanye West, covering his early career at Roc-A-Fella Records, the 2005 Hurricane Katrina benefit controversy, and his mother Donda West's death after cosmetic surgery in November 2007. It also covers his DONDA creative company, his co-ownership of the Tidal streaming service, his controversial 2013 Kazakhstan performance and remarks, a 2006 trademark lawsuit by Robert Evel Knievel, and the artists who have cited him as an influence.
one_line: Excerpts from Kanye West's Wikipedia article covering his career controversies, his mother's death, DONDA, Tidal ownership, and artistic influence.
key_facts: Damon Dash reluctantly signed Kanye West to Roc-A-Fella Records after West nearly signed with Capitol Records.
Jay-Z later admitted that Roc-A-Fella was initially reluctant to support West as a rapper because many saw him as a producer first.
In September 2005, West said on NBC's A Concert for Hurricane Relief, "George Bush doesn't care about black people."
President Bush later called the comment one of the most "disgusting moments" of his presidency.
Donda West died on November 10, 2007, at age 58 at Centinela Freeman Hospital in Marina del Rey, California.
The final coroner's report of January 10, 2008, concluded that Donda West died of "coronary artery disease and multiple post-operative factors" linked to liposuction and mammoplasty.
Jan Adams performed the procedures on Donda West after Beverly Hills surgeon Andre Aboolian refused to operate due to heart risk.
On January 5, 2012, West announced the creative content company DONDA, named after his late mother.
On March 30, 2015, it was announced that West was a co-owner of the music streaming service Tidal.
Jay-Z acquired the parent company of Tidal, Aspiro, in the first quarter of 2015.
In September 2013, West performed in Kazakhstan at the wedding of President Nursultan Nazarbayev's grandson and was reportedly paid US$3 million.
On November 26, 2013, West said in a radio interview that Obama lacked the connections of Jewish people, prompting a rebuke from the Anti-Defamation League.
On December 21, 2013, West said of his comment that "if anything it came off more ignorant."
In December 2006, Robert "Evel" Knievel sued West for trademark infringement over the music video for "Touch the Sky"; Knievel settled the suit days before his death in November 2007.
In February 2016, West posted a tweet seemingly asserting Bill Cosby's innocence amid sexual assault allegations by over 50 women.
